title: d-6: sqlite-storage
description:
## Deliverables
1. Implement SQLite's share of the one shared sc-storage Storage<T> trait and its single AtomicStorage::transaction(spec, producer) operation for several row operations as one atomic unit; SQLite (d-6), Postgres (d-7) and MySQL (d-8) each implement that same contract (ANC-032/033). Implement the shared sc-storage Storage<T> trait and its generic transaction operation that runs several row operations as one atomic unit over a bounded channel whose design is adapted from atm-core (copied code, no dependency), single writer and reader pool. The writer thread exclusively owns the only write-mode SQLite connection; reader workers open read-only connections. Futures are NEW work, not copied typed operations. Read-write body is one writer message/savepoint; queue batches commit together and replies follow commit. Read-only may use reader pool — REQ-DBSQ-0002/0003; ANC-022..027/033.
2. Enforce transaction-body non-suspension: Pending rolls back with typed error, failed/panicked body never commits. Public storage APIs return typed Result and never panic; writer panic terminates/fails every pending/in-flight/queued caller without hangs — NFR-RUN-0002; ANC-035/036. Qualify actual external analyzer/no-panic rules for changed code, never substitute runtime polling for static analysis.
3. Generic row/migration/codec implementation contains no cron/application table type, schema or SQL. Consumer supplies row descriptors; all consumer policies live above storage. No sc-cron dependency/feature — ANC-032/034. Consume real row/options/codec declarations frozen in d-5; implement the concrete database API, with no duplicate definitions.
4. Use the shared root rusqlite requirement >=0.41 with no upper bound; run the normal SQLite test suite. Thin generated SQLite storage consumes the generic backend and application-owned schema and removes SQLx SQLite/cache/config — REQ-DBSQ-0001; REQ-RUN-0308; ANC-061/028/037.

5. Retire the public raw-SQL SqliteWriter/WriterConn/SqlValue/SqliteWriterError facade in0.3.0; raw connection/execute helpers become crate-private behind generic Storage<T>. Implement inherent SqliteDatabase open/storage/shutdown/wait_closed with SqliteOpenOptions, not a factory trait. Amend REQ-DBSQ-0001/0002 and its architecture/boundary public facade to the final implemented dependency/API surface, following d-5 declarations. All owned registry requirements use >= tested floors without upper bounds (ANC-037).

## Boundaries and handoffs
Cron schema/domain policy/migration are d-9; real cron conformance and complete generated/mixed layouts are d-11; actual upstream/publication d-12. Backend tests use generic rows and do not contain a CronRow codec or cron SQL.
This sprint implements Storage<T> for SqliteStore<T> using that shared trait, with no SQLite-specific parallel storage trait; it implements the SAME AtomicStorage::transaction(spec, producer) method as one writer message/savepoint.
After the d-5 boundary registration handoff, own boundaries/sc-runtime-db-sqlite/sc-runtime-db-sqlite.toml for the actual public-facade/root removals matching this implementation. This is the boundary's own facade, not a shared root registry.

These phase-d transaction-body rules do not prohibit later second transform inputs, typed Ok/no-write outcomes or a transform inside an atomic transaction; those behaviors are not built in this sprint (ANC-051).
design:
Consumes the real d-5 factory/codec/Storage/transaction declarations and prototype result. Own implementation after explicit staged manifest/lib.rs handoff; no redefinition of contract.rs. The writer thread exclusively owns the only write-mode SQLite connection; one database handle routes writes through its queue, and reader workers use read-only connections. Copy only proven channel/reader plumbing from atm-core, implement the new future mechanism with explicit prototype risk. Per root writer constraints, only writer runtime drives Runtime::block_on; readers use blocking_recv, no runtime.
Read-write transaction producer executes in one savepoint inside queued outer transaction; failed/suspended body rolls back that savepoint, outer commit precedes success reply. Owned Send+'static producer creates a fresh future per attempt; SQLite body can await only tx operations. Actual Pending is rejected, even if a call would later become ready. Runtime is not the analyzer. Worker catch_unwind translates panic to typed worker-failed state, drains/fails every outstanding reply and closes admission; subsequent callers get typed failure. No public API panics.
No table-specific code or dependency on sc-cron. Storage<T> uses registered generic descriptor/codec; application chooses/migrates schema through generic engine API. d-6 removes SQLx SQLite only in its owned store wrapper manifest after d-5 additive registration. Package/default features remain consumer-neutral. Direct native identity is proved by cargo tree -i libsqlite3-sys; absence of sqlx-sqlite by cargo tree, not lockfile. Generic backend/native mix compile probes are boundary evidence, not complete generated app proof.
The d-5-owned root already registers rusqlite >=0.41; this sprint does not edit Cargo.toml. Only SqliteDatabase/Store<T> typed APIs are public; raw connection/SQL machinery is private. wait_closed returns typed completion/failure for existing daemon shutdown control.
acceptance_criteria:
boundary:sc-runtime-db-sqlite — Run shared generic-row/atomic conformance on real SQLite, including create-generated-key/delete primitives for the d-5-frozen, owner-ratified template extension, transaction rollback, queue admission, batching/commit-before-reply, read-only pool, shutdown and typed errors. No table-specific backend source; no cron dependency/SQL/schema. The writer thread exclusively owns the only write-mode SQLite connection; readers use read-only connections (ANC-023). All changed public storage functions return Result and do not panic.
boundary:sc-runtime-db-sqlite/unsafe-body — Controlled future returns Pending: rollback + typed suspension error, no commit. Inject a writer/body panic after admitting multiple requests; await all registered replies and verify every one receives typed error, admission closes and no caller is left hanging. Drive controlled poll/barrier/channel states, no sleeps/time-race assertions. Runtime tests reject actual suspension. The actual analyzer must reject awaits on non-transaction handles and calls to unmarked helpers; record external rule state honestly.
boundary:sc-runtime-db-sqlite/dependencies — Run the normal real SQLite/atomic test suite. cargo tree -i libsqlite3-sys shows one selected version>=0.39 and -i sqlx-sqlite selects no package; check the resolved graph, not Cargo.lock. No ATM/sc-compose composition-crate release dependencies; sc-sha is permitted (ANC-061).
Required: cargo test -p sc-runtime-db-sqlite --all-features; cargo clippy -p sc-runtime-db-sqlite --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings; cargo build --workspace at this closure; sc-lint lint sc-boundary --root . --config sc-lint.toml; sc-lint#931 no-panic rule and the external transaction-body analyzer must pass on this sprint's changed storage code once delivered; until both rules exist and pass, closure stays blocked. Record the actual rule versions and commands when available, never a fabricated pass or implicit waiver. Wrapper tests use real SQLite/generic contracts; d-11 owns full generated composition.
Use d-5's transaction observation wrapper with controlled observer tests (ANC-033).
boundary:sc-runtime-db-sqlite/callers — Async callers submit through the channel and await replies without blocking their thread or using spawn_blocking to submit writes; controlled admission/reply tests exercise this path (ANC-027).
notes: authored from docs/prd/sc-runtime-prd.md and ADR0020/0021@a6cc949bafa9e7f1817f4514a19328c3021ffc42; B selected via lead01M76Q2R5JRAE3AA9NVBEF1HG4, placement/service cut via01M76Q74CR889863W7EHRW2A14; original d-1/d-3 work folded into named owners, no overlapping A sprint

metadata.vertical_rationale: One generic SQLite implementation plus table-neutral generated forwarding crate. Application/cron table mapping and policy live in schema/service/sc-cron, not storage backends; no second engine implementation or standalone thin sprint.

dependencies.title: Phase D: shared app storage, channel writer and published consumer migration
dependencies.description:
Phase D makes the SDK easy to adopt and lets consumers choose dependency upgrades. Product intent is PRD v2.0; the release is the owner-selected nine public crates at0.3.0. Generic backends contain no consumer table code. Sprint metadata.owned_paths is the authoritative full file fence; summaries below are navigation only.

| Sprint | Wave | Boundary | Consumed artifacts |
|---|---|---|---|
| d-3 | 1 | dependency/source compatibility | none; owns the one manifest checker |
| d-4 | 1 | generation tooling | none |
| d-5 | 1 | storage/atomic/row contract + standalone sc-monty | none; owner ratification and Active ADR0020/0021 before consumers |
| d-6 | 2 | SQLite backend | d-5 production contract |
| d-7 | 2 | Postgres backend | d-5 production contract |
| d-8 | 2 | MySQL backend | d-5 production contract |
| d-9 | 2 | cron domain adapter | d-5 production contract and additive legacy build |
| d-10 | 2 | common commands/transforms | d-3 compiled command server/schema/error ABI, d-5 Storage/row contract |
| d-11 | 3 | generated composition | d-3 checker, d-4 tools, d-6/7/8/9/10 code |
| d-12 | 3 | registry migration/release/recommendations | d-3 source/checker, d-4 tools, d-6/9/10 code; d-11 completion checked before upload |

Ten sprints; critical path3, width6. No dependency exists solely because two sprints edit the same manifest. The release and generated-integration sprints prepare in parallel; upload waits for completed generated integration. No implementation dispatch before plan approval.
dependencies.design:
PRD v2.0 governs product scope. sc-storage is std-only; storage/atomic/row traits are the shared contract, with phase-d transaction name/mode properties and room for later per-transaction retry policy. SQLite uses one async queue and one writer thread exclusively owning its sole write-mode connection, queued writes commit together, and replies follow commit. Only the writer runtime uses Runtime::block_on. Readers use blocking_recv without a runtime; async callers never block or use spawn_blocking to submit writes. Consumer rows/schema/migrations stay above generic engines. sc-cron implements its policy once over generic atomic Storage<CronRow> and keeps raw backend mutation out of the CronStore public facade.

D-5 owns contract types, shared registry/boundary definitions, required REQ/ADR amendments and the minimal legacy compatibility build. Its layer-file handoffs are additive contract/legacy artifacts on existing dependencies, not simultaneous same-wave edits. d-9 owns the0.3.0 removal of ScheduleStore/SqliteScheduleStore and obsolete SQLite files after those artifacts compile. Root Cargo.toml passes directly from d-5 registrations to d-12 release-version conversion; d-6 reads it. d-3 owns the command manifest with its rmcp3.9 server/schema compatibility code; d-10 consumes that compiled artifact and later adds storage helpers. Specific crate facade boundaries pass from d-5 to their implementation owner on the existing must-follow edges.

D-5 owner ratification is pending and gates its closure; ADR0020/0021 must be Active before d-6..d-12 start. The actual no-panic rule sc-lint#931 and transaction-safe analyzer remain required for affected owner-sprint closure and are rechecked before publication. Lead owns the external analyzer request; missing delivery is a real blocker, not a waiver.

D-3 owns the sole interim SDK manifest checker; d-11 invokes it on generated outputs and d-12 on exact archives/upload. Remove it after equivalent sc-lint#936 release/adoption. Published/template registry requirements are open tested floors (ANC-037); normal tests check the selected versions, with no dedicated min/latest jobs. Consumers may pin what they want. D-12 alone produces the final newest-tested Cargo.lock recommendation and matching .sc-runtime/tested-dependencies.json (ANC-038).

Nine published packages at0.3.0: sc-storage, sc-runtime-db-sqlite, sc-config, sc-transport, sc-command, sc-runtime, sc-cron, sc-cron-commands, sc-monty. Postgres/MySQL generic engines remain generated this phase under that approved packaging scope; their implementation fixes need template updates/regeneration, explicitly recorded in ADR0020. They do not acquire an invented library-upgrade guarantee. D-12 derives publication order from actual manifests, sc-monty/sc-storage in the first wave, rehearses exact archives, then proves actual upstream beads-cache PR open/CI green against registry crates. Its independent preparation does not upload until d-11 sanity is closed and completed composition merged, with ratification and actual safety rules passing. Missing release predicates leave publication open.

The phase is one append-only stack with one writer. Metadata layer is planned presentation order; actual link order follows completion. pr_target is the consumed lower bound, not false sibling serialization. Canonical root Cargo.lock is d-12-owned. Historical probe facts remain in Git/review evidence, not a second live scope document.


## Boundary map and generated targets
Read existing boundaries/<crate>/<crate>.toml. sc-config dependencies serde/serde_json unchanged; sc-transport tokio/reqwest/serde->sc-runtime unchanged; sc-command gains sc-storage, consumers sc-cron/sc-cron-commands/sc-runtime; sc-runtime composes transport/command, no storage trait placement there; sc-cron loses direct SQLite backend, depends on sc-storage/sc-command; sc-cron-commands adapts scheduler. Generic writer dependencies sc-storage/rusqlite/Tokio only, NEVER sc-cron/ATM/sc-compose; no consumer SQL/schema. New boundaries/sc-storage/sc-storage.toml has no sc-* dependency. Generated store/service boundaries are emitted by template/boundaries/render.py at boundaries/<prefixed-package>/<prefixed-package>.toml with existing Store/Stores facades; no invented static template boundaries. Application row descriptors/migrations are supplied at open, engine applies them before exposing store.

Wave-1 d-5 delivers the single sc-monty implementation, first copying current code and all unit/integration tests exactly and passing them before extension. Its production dependencies are only pydantic Monty crates; sc-cron owns cron/JSON adapters and source-keyed compiled-session blobs via generic Storage rows, sc-sha is permitted. d-11 follows the existing d-9/d-10 prerequisites to route cron.start/end/list through common helpers and a library-owned policy adapter, without bypassing CronStorage or requiring app-written actions. Transform sources load at run time, default conversion needs no hand-written transform, and the provisional0.3.0 seam preserves future second-input/no-write/atomic-transform options without building them.
dependencies.acceptance_criteria:
1. d-11 closes actual generated SQLite app/cron shared database/channel writer, real typed transforms/CRUD and all selected engines/mixed layouts; no vulnerable SQLx SQLite or separate cron.db default, no fake engine proof.
2. d-12 closes actual upstream migration PR open/CI-green at exact SHA against nine published0.3.0 crates; no path/patch/Git SDK substitute. All source/package/API/docs and normal test suites pass.
3. Generic backends contain no consumer table code; named owned retryable atomic API and static+runtime safety checks actually operate. Public changed storage APIs return typed errors/no panic; writer panic fails every waiting caller. External rule and ratification blockers stay explicit until met.
4. All existing workspace/lint/test/boundary/publishing-kit/controlled-host benchmark gates pass; publication waits for closed d-11 sanity and owner ratification, after exact archive rehearsal. Required coverage and independent plan/development gates are separate from schema validation.
